title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 354 (Meetings to ascertain wishes of creditors or contributories)

content.overview: In all matters relating to the winding up of a company, the Tribunal may have regard to the wishes of creditors or contributories of the company as proved to it by any sufficient evidence, and may, if it thinks fit for the purpose of ascertaining those wishes, direct meetings of the creditors or contributories to be called, held and conducted in such manner as the Tribunal directs, and may appoint a person to act as chairman of any such meeting and to report the result thereof to the Tribunal. In the case of creditors, regard shall be had to the value of each creditor’s debt; in the case of contributories, to the number of votes conferred on each contributory by the Act or the articles.
content.glance: Tribunal may have regard to wishes of creditors/contributories, direct meetings to ascertain those wishes, and appoint a chairman; weighting by debt value or voting rights.
content.study: Section 354 empowers the Tribunal, in all matters relating to winding up, to have regard to the wishes of creditors or contributories as proved by sufficient evidence, and to direct meetings for that purpose. The Tribunal may appoint a chairman and require a report of the result. Creditor wishes are weighted by the value of each debt; contributory wishes by the number of votes conferred by the Act or the articles.

sections.heading: Regard to wishes and meetings
sections.body: Tribunal may regard wishes of creditors/contributories and direct meetings; chairman may be appointed; weighting by debt value or votes.

provisions.title: Meetings to ascertain wishes of creditors or contributories

examples.title: Creditors’ meeting directed
examples.body: On a contested application concerning asset realisation strategy, the Tribunal under s. 354 directs a meeting of creditors, weighted by debt value, and appoints a chairman to report.

hypotheticals.question: Must the Tribunal always call a meeting before deciding a winding-up matter?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The Tribunal may have regard to wishes as proved by sufficient evidence and may direct meetings if it thinks fit; meetings are discretionary.

misconceptions.trap: Creditor and contributory votes are counted per head only.
misconceptions.correction: Creditor wishes are weighted by debt value; contributory wishes by statutory or article voting rights.
